the data quality of the datasets archived in Ecology and Evolution and Evolution journals is low, with only 36% being complete and 36% being archived in a way to enable reuse.
56% of the datasets surveyed were incomplete, 64% were not archived in a way allowing reuse, and 64–100% (depending on the dataset) were not archived in the most efficient way.
56% of data are incomplete and 64% of datasets are archived in a way preventing reuse.

the quality of data archived by authors and the extent to which the data are accessible to the scientific community.
data sharing and data archiving in ecology and evolution.
the quality of publicly available data in ecology and evolution, and how to increase the reuse potential of these data.

the current state of PDA in ecology and evolution is not satisfactory.
we are still far from the ideal situation of all data being reusable.
the quality of public data archiving in the field of ecology and evolutionary biology is not yet sufficient for the data to be reusable.

the data quality is not good enough to allow reuse and reproducibility.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PDA policies are not enough to guarantee high-quality archiving of data.
